page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. It features 16 physical cores supporting 32 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 64.0 GB, maintaining a 1:2 ratio of vCPU to RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU). The instance is deployed on KVM hypervisors, provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, includes no local storage, and contains zero discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that multi-core processing performance falls into the middle tier, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 31611.76 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 12260.17. Single-threaded capability demonstrates performance limitations, recording a low stress-ng single-core score of 766.88. Uncached memory bandwidth tests display weak throughput at 35.37 GB/sec for reads and 16.73 GB/sec for writes, whereas cached memory throughput reaches 1571.99 GB/sec.

From a hardware allocation perspective, the 32 dedicated vCPUs provide consistent computational resources without the added overhead of bundled local storage. Web serving throughput reaches 7.74 GB/sec and Redis SET performance registers at 27.12 million operations per second. This profile suits multi-threaded application workloads, software compilation pipelines, web server layers, and distributed caching nodes where multi-core execution is prioritized over single-thread speed or localized storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical AMD EPYC 7H12 cores running at 2.6 GHz, accompanied by 64.0 GB of memory. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, this instance features an 8 Gbps network bandwidth baseline without included local disk storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmark results reveal average multi-core processing performance, exemplified by a PassMark CPU score of 31611.76 and multi-threaded stress-ng score of 12260.17, while single-core processing and uncached memory bandwidth show weaker relative metrics. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance offers efficient compute density for workloads that rely heavily on parallel processing rather than single-threaded speed. This hardware profile is well suited for software compilation, web serving, Redis caching nodes, and parallel batch processing applications.
